### Bug Scenario and Root Cause

The bug scenario involves a Lighthouse report showing a `NO_TTI_CPU_IDLE_PERIOD` error when the page has a slow First Contentful Paint (FCP) but becomes idle immediately after. This error occurs because Lighthouse is unable to find a sufficient period of CPU idleness after the FCP, which is required to calculate the Time to Interactive (TTI) metric. The error is visible in the performance metrics section of the Lighthouse report, where 'Time to Interactive' and 'Total Blocking Time' show errors due to the lack of a CPU idle period.

### Bug Location and Analysis

The issue is located in the `lighthouse-core/computed/metrics/interactive.js` file. The function `findOverlappingQuietPeriods` is responsible for identifying periods of network and CPU idleness. The error is thrown when no overlapping quiet periods are found, which is the case when the page becomes idle immediately after a slow FCP.

### Patches

To address this issue, we can adjust the logic to handle cases where the page becomes idle immediately after FCP. We can modify the `findOverlappingQuietPeriods` function to ensure it accounts for this scenario.
